all_candidates.topic: Should student protests directly influence government legislative decisions?
all_candidates.news_anchor: Youth-led protests over exam paper leaks, culminating last week, directly influenced the government's decision to pass the anti-paper leak bill.

all_candidates.topic: Should new anti-leak law penalties deter exam cheats?
all_candidates.news_anchor: India's Lok Sabha passed the Public Examinations (Prevention of Unfair Means) Amendment Bill, 2026 on July 29, 2026, proposing significantly tougher penalties for paper leaks.

all_candidates.topic: Does stricter punishment address root causes of exam leaks?
all_candidates.news_anchor: The Public Examinations (Prevention of Unfair Means) Amendment Bill, 2026, introducing stricter penalties, was passed by Lok Sabha on July 29, 2026.

all_candidates.topic: Is strengthening India's anti-cheating law the right approach?
all_candidates.news_anchor: India's Lok Sabha passed the Public Examinations (Prevention of Unfair Means) Amendment Bill, 2026 on July 29, 2026, strengthening an existing 2024 law.

all_candidates.topic: Should consumer commissions impose stricter penalties for faulty products?
all_candidates.news_anchor: A Punjab Consumer Commission ordered Whirlpool to pay a refund for a malfunctioning AC on July 27, 2026, holding the company liable for deficiency of service.

all_candidates.topic: Should consumers always have a choice between E20 and conventional fuels?
all_candidates.news_anchor: A satirical 'E20 Janta Party' account went viral on July 27, 2026, advocating for motorists to have the option to choose their preferred petrol blend.

all_candidates.topic: Does satirical online activism effectively influence policy changes?
all_candidates.news_anchor: The 'Cockroach Janta Party' movement, utilizing satirical online activism, played a significant role in recent student protests which led to the Education Minister's resignation.

all_candidates.topic: Is integrating youth slang into parliamentary debates beneficial?
all_candidates.news_anchor: Gen Z terms like 'Vasteguna Huiya' and 'Kuchu Puchu' were mentioned in a Parliament debate on July 28, 2026, related to the anti-paper leak bill.

all_candidates.topic: Should daily fuel price changes be replaced by less frequent revisions?
all_candidates.news_anchor: NITI Aayog Vice Chairman Ashok Lahiri stated on July 26, 2026, that fuel prices will be revised only after a sustained decline in crude oil prices, not with frequent fluctuations.

all_candidates.topic: Will fast-track courts improve exam leak justice?
all_candidates.news_anchor: The Public Examinations (Prevention of Unfair Means) Amendment Bill, 2026, passed on July 29, 2026, also proposes special fast-track courts for exam malpractice cases.

all_candidates.topic: Will new anti-leak law face significant implementation hurdles?
all_candidates.news_anchor: The Public Examinations Amendment Bill 2026, passed on July 29, 2026, with tougher penalties, is reported to face implementation hurdles and backlog challenges.

all_candidates.topic: Does ministerial accountability boost public trust in governance?
all_candidates.news_anchor: Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan resigned last week (around July 25-26, 2026) following nationwide protests over exam paper leaks and irregularities.

all_candidates.topic: Will India's new EV policy successfully boost domestic manufacturing?
all_candidates.news_anchor: India's government unveiled a new Electric Vehicle (EV) policy on July 28, 2026, emphasizing structural reforms and manufacturing support to foster a robust EV ecosystem.

all_candidates.topic: Is the PM-eBus Sewa scheme sufficient for urban transport needs?
all_candidates.news_anchor: The government sanctioned 10,000 electric buses under the PM-eBus Sewa Scheme on July 27, 2026, to augment city bus services.

all_candidates.topic: Will new TRP policy rules genuinely improve data credibility?
all_candidates.news_anchor: The 'TRP 2026 policy' was recently unveiled, tightening rules to sharpen data credibility in viewership ratings.

all_candidates.topic: Is the new urea investment policy vital for India's self-sufficiency?
all_candidates.news_anchor: The Cabinet recently approved a new urea investment policy to establish 8-9 gas-based plants, aiming for self-sufficiency by 2026.

all_candidates.topic: Will new e-commerce export reforms significantly boost MSME growth?
all_candidates.news_anchor: India's latest e-commerce export reforms, aimed at transforming MSMEs into global exporters, were announced on July 24, 2026.

all_candidates.topic: Will Arunachal Pradesh's new schemes significantly boost rural connectivity?
all_candidates.news_anchor: The Arunachal Pradesh Cabinet recently approved ₹7,834 crore for four major schemes, including investments to improve roads and rural connectivity.

all_candidates.topic: Is a dedicated Department of Military Medicine beneficial for armed forces?
all_candidates.news_anchor: The first dedicated Department of Military Medicine recently came up in Lucknow.

all_candidates.topic: Will the new mine reform scheme boost mineral production adequately?
all_candidates.news_anchor: The Centre recently rolled out a ₹5,175 crore mine reform incentive scheme (SASCI 2026-27) to accelerate mine operationalization and boost mineral production.
